reason: Both conversations deliver an essentially identical and correct safety stop (stop using, don't reset, unplug, get an engineer), and both fail to ask the key triage questions (does the RCD hold with it unplugged, extension lead, door closing) or mention that a cheap 5-year-old solo microwave is probably a replace-not-repair case. Conversation 1 edges ahead because it names the door interlock switch as a possible cause, which matches the likely hidden fault, whereas Conversation 2 points only at high-voltage components. Conversation 2's explicit 'do not open the casing' warning is a small safety plus, but the homeowner already won't open it and both responses route them to a professional, so it does not outweigh the more accurate diagnostic direction in 1.
